question: Were woolly mammoths still alive somewhere on Earth when the Great Pyramid of Giza was built?

claims.text: Woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until roughly 2000 BCE.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around 2560 BCE.
Wrangel mammoths were alive for about 500 years after pyramid construction began.
Radiocarbon dating of Wrangel remains places the last survivors well after the pyramid's construction.
The Wrangel population was isolated by rising sea levels and persisted long after mainland mammoths vanished.
The question only requires one surviving population somewhere on Earth.
Mainland mammoths died out about 10,000 years ago and St. Paul Island mammoths about 5,600 years ago, so most of the species was gone by the pyramid era.
Radiocarbon error margins and some earlier extinction estimates for Wrangel could weaken the overlap.
Even with earlier Wrangel estimates, the overlap with 2560 BCE would likely remain.
Uncertainty of a few decades in the pyramid's date does not change the conclusion.
The mainland and St. Paul extinctions are irrelevant once Wrangel survival past 2560 BCE is shown.
